brief:
A disconnect between top Democratic leaders and the party base over Israel policy is shaping internal party battles, Mondoweiss reported. Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries hold positions at odds with significant portions of Democratic voters on the issue, raising questions about whether the disagreement could prompt shifts in party leadership.

The tension reflects broader fractures within the Democratic coalition on Middle East policy. Whether this ideological gap translates into actual leadership changes remains uncertain, but the conflict signals deeper questions about Democratic party direction and representation of its members' views.
dek: Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries are out of step with the Democratic base on Israel. Can that disconnect fuel a leadership change?
title: Democratic leadership divide over Israel deepens party rift
